modelGuidance:
Luna is the lowest-cost, fastest model in this workflow. Use it for token-intensive work that requires gathering, filtering, or organizing evidence but little independent judgment. Typical uses include browser interaction, web research, session-history retrieval, broad inventories, and extracting facts from many files or records. It is the only model allowed to use browser tools. Luna should report evidence, source locations, and coverage gaps rather than make consequential technical decisions from incomplete evidence.

Sol is the balanced general-purpose model. It is more appropriate than Luna when the task requires understanding code, applying a repository's existing patterns, or synthesizing evidence, but does not justify the additional cost and latency of Fable or Astra. Use Sol as the normal starting point for engineering work.

Fable is the strongest model for complex planning, architecture design, implementation, and code writing. Use it when difficult engineering work benefits from deeper reasoning and the additional cost and latency are justified.

Astra is available as an independent perspective for reviewing and verifying complex work. Consider it when challenging assumptions, assessing architectural or behavioral risks, or verifying consequential plans or implementations would be genuinely valuable, especially for work produced by Fable. Do not use Astra or pair models merely to increase agent count.
